message:
fix(host): a cached token meant the advertisement never arrived

A host that had registered before starts with a token, so EnsureRegistered
returns immediately -- and the observe advertisement only ever arrived on the
registration response. On https there is no default to fall back to, so the
host could not aim its observation, could not heartbeat, and never appeared
in anyone's list. It sat at directory=pending with a perfectly good token and
a perfectly good server.

The better the previous run went, the more certainly the next one was stuck.

The health route already answered this question and needs no session. It was
in the viewer's file, which is why the host had no way to ask it: ten targets
link the directory client and do not link the session client. The
implementation moved, and the viewer's function now delegates to it, so there
is one of it.

The trigger is "we are guessing", not "we have nowhere to aim". On https the
absence is loud. On http the guess is httpPort + 1, which resolves and then
points at nobody if the server listens elsewhere -- an aim that looks like it
worked. Both ask; the answer is only used if one comes back. Nothing pinned
by an operator is overridden, and in that case the route is not asked at all.

Bounded, not polled: six attempts with a growing cooldown. A directory that
has not been configured yet may be configured later, so asking again is
right; asking every twenty-five seconds forever turns a server-side omission
into traffic nobody looks at.

And the specific reason was being overwritten. "Address observation timed
out" was set whenever the observation failed, including when the real problem
was that we had nowhere to send it -- turning a server configuration message
into a network symptom. It is only used now when there was somewhere to aim.

The regression drives the real HostAgent from a seeded cache. The fake
directory's observe port is one the OS picked, so it is not httpPort + 1 and
the legacy default cannot reach it: a heartbeat is itself the evidence that
the advertisement was fetched and used. Removing the fix again turns five of
those assertions red.
